candidate.title: OAuth `state` is `pipeline.signature`, a global constant — the CSRF check is decorative
candidate.description: Pipeline.signature is an md5 hash of constant pipeline view class names, identical for all users and stable across deploys. Attacker can exploit by installing the GitHub App on a controlled org, then luring a Sentry admin to `/extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker_code>&state=<constant>`, causing the victim's pipeline to bind the attacker's GitHub user and connect their installation to the victim's org.

gold.description: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation

candidate.title: `integration.metadata["sender"]` raises `KeyError` for pipeline-created integrations
candidate.description: The `sender` key in metadata only exists for webhook-created integrations, not pipeline-created ones. Re-installing after disconnection hits unhandled KeyError at line 503 instead of showing the failure dialog.

promotion_candidates.title: `test_installation_not_found` no longer tests installation-not-found
promotion_candidates.description: Test uses incorrect state parameter that doesn't match pipeline.signature, causing request to error at state check before reaching `build_integration`. The installation-not-found error path is now uncovered.

promotion_candidates.title: `Integration` fetched twice for the same `external_id`
promotion_candidates.description: Integration is queried twice: at line 478 without status filter, then at line 494 with ACTIVE status filter. Redundant round-trip, and status condition split across blocks causes non-ACTIVE integrations to silently take the generic error path.
